hints.title: Skill-Sorted Job Traversal
hints.text: Sort jobs by required skill and maintain the running maximum reward available up to each difficulty level.

hints.title: Sorted Worker Assignment
hints.text: Sort workers ascending by ability so a single pointer can track available jobs.

hints.title: Running Best Profit Tracking
hints.text: As worker capacity increases, advance the job index while job difficulty is within capacity and update the best profit observed so far.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxProfitAssignment(self, difficulty: List[int], profit: List[int], worker: List[int]) -> int:
        jobs = sorted(zip(difficulty, profit))
        worker.sort()
        ans = 0
        max_profit = 0
        i = 0
        n = len(jobs)

        for ability in worker:
            while i < n and jobs[i][0] <= ability:
                if jobs[i][1] > max_profit:
                    max_profit = jobs[i][1]
                i += 1
            ans += max_profit

        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(J log J + W log W)
complexity.notes: Sorts jobs and workers followed by synchronized two-pointer traversal.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all jobs for each worker takes O(J * W) time, which times out.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of paired tuples takes O(J) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use monotonic two-pointer scan over sorted jobs and sorted workers.
